title: March flow gave no clear added May-July flow forecast gain at three Arctic gauges in 28 certified years from 1983 to 2011
abstract: We tested whether March mean flow improves May-July flow forecasts beyond calendar year and previous-year May-July flow at Ob-Salekhard, Lena-Kyusyur and Yenisey-Igarka. We used ArcticGRO v20261104, certified seasonal records, and fits with earlier years only. In 28 common test years from 1983 to 2011, the equal-river mean reduction in mean squared error was -4.70%. The conditional 95% three-year block range was -16.95% to +4.98%. Thus the test gave no clear added gain. All four planned checks also had ranges that included zero. The point reduction was -13.98% at Ob, +3.87% at Lena and -3.97% at Yenisey. This tests one form of winter-to-spring forecast information, not a causal storage mechanism. Revised data, retrospective certification, regulation, a short historical test, model choice and conditional uncertainty limit use. Original code, source hashes, aggregate evidence, an arithmetic audit and a figure support reproduction. Raw and record-level derived data remain external.

display.caption: Added March flow gave no clear May-July forecast gain. Left: equal-river scores and planned checks. Right: primary river scores. Ranges are conditional block-bootstrap 95% ranges; river ranges are pointwise.

citations.reason: Winter flow ratios and autumn adjustment motivate a forecast test with trend and past-flow controls. Same source, different target and method.
Related chronological seasonal forecast test. We test March flow for May-July volume at three gauges, rather than spring timing for later summer flow at Lena.
Fixed source v20261104; Arctic Great Rivers Observatory and Roshydromet.
